2_Introduction: The champion device showed a PCE of 20.8695%, with JSC of 22.991 mA/cm², FF of 80.244%, and VOC of 1.1312 V. 1.5 mol/L Cs0.1FA0.9PbI2.8Br0.2 perovskite precursors were prepared. To establish a stable perovskite film, the substrate was spun at 1200 rpm for 10 s, then at 5000 rpm for 30 s, ensuring even layer formation. 200 µL CB was dropped onto the substrate during the last 8 s of the spinning, resulting in the formation of dark brown films. It was then heated at 110 °C for 30 min, resulting in the formation of the perovskite thin films.
3_Result_Discussion: The Cs₀.₁FA₀.₉PbI₂.₈Br₀.₂ perovskite composition leverages the synergistic A-site cation engineering of formamidinium (FA⁺) for optimal bandgap tuning (~1.53 eV) and phase stability, while partial cesium (Cs⁺) substitution enhances the Goldschmidt tolerance factor (≈0.98), suppresses δ-phase formation, and mitigates halide segregation and ion migration under operational stress; the precisely controlled precursor concentration (1.5 mol/L) balances nucleation density and growth kinetics, where the two-step spin-coating protocol—initial low-speed (1200 rpm, 10 s) for wet-film uniformity followed by high-speed (5000 rpm, 30 s) for solvent evaporation control—enables reproducible thickness and interfacial contact, and the timed antisolvent quenching with 200 µL chlorobenzene during the final 8 s critically arrests intermediate solvate phase evolution, promoting rapid, homogeneous nucleation of the α-phase while minimizing PbI₂-rich grain boundaries and pinhole formation; subsequent thermal annealing at 110 °C for 30 min drives complete ligand expulsion and crystal coalescence, reducing trap-assisted recombination and enhancing carrier diffusion length—evidenced by high-contrast, uniformly dark brown films indicating near-complete surface coverage and minimal light-scattering defects, corroborated by strong, spatially homogeneous photoluminescence intensity and monoexponential decay kinetics consistent with low non-radiative recombination and suppressed trap states, while XRD analysis confirms dominant (110) α-phase peaks with negligible residual PbI₂ (absence of ~12.6° peak) and narrow FWHM, reflecting high crystallinity, low microstrain, and phase purity; collectively, these crystallization dynamics yield a dense, pinhole-free polycrystalline film with reduced deep-level defects at grain boundaries and surfaces, enabling efficient charge extraction and minimal voltage losses, resulting in VOC of 1.1312 V, JSC of 22.991 mA/cm², FF of 80.244%, and PCE of 20.8695%.
